translation_en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, who said that Muhammad said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah reported from his father that on that day the Prophet sat on a camel, while a man held its reins—or its bridle—and he related something similar to the hadith of Yazid ibn Zuray'.

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah and another man whom I consider better than him. In another chain, Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Jablah and Ahmad ibn Kharash narrated from Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, from Qurrah, with Yahya ibn Sa'id's chain, naming the man as Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Bakrah. He said: The Messenger of Allah addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice and asked, 'What day is this?' They narrated the hadith like Ibn 'Awn's, except they did not mention your honor or the part about turning to two rams and what followed. He said, 'Like the inviolability of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours, until the day you meet your Lord. Have I conveyed the message?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'O Allah, bear witness.'

' Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Abu Yunus narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that 'Alqamah ibn Wa'il told him that his father told him: I was sitting with the Prophet when a man came leading another by a leather strap and said, Messenger of Allah, this man killed my brother. The Messenger of Allah asked, Did you kill him? He replied, If he had not confessed, I would have established proof against him. The man said, Yes, I killed him. He asked how. The man said, He and I were cutting leaves from a tree. He insulted me and angered me, so I struck him with an axe on the side of his head and killed him. The Prophet asked whether he had anything to offer as ransom. He said he owned only his garment and axe. The Prophet asked if his people would buy his freedom. He replied that he was too insignificant to them. The Prophet tossed him the strap and said, Take your companion. The man led him away. When he turned his back, the Messenger of Allah said, If he kills him, he will be like him. The man returned and said he had taken him by the Prophet's command. The Messenger of Allah asked, Do you not want him to bear your sin and your companion's sin? He said perhaps yes. The Prophet replied, That is indeed so. The man threw down the strap and released him.

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Salim informed us, from 'Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from his father, who said: A man who had killed another was brought to the Messenger of Allah, and he handed the slain man's heir authority to retaliate. The heir went off with the man, a leather strap around his neck, dragging him. When he had gone away, the Messenger of Allah said, The killer and the one killed are in the Fire. A man came to the heir and told him what the Messenger of Allah had said, so he let the man go. Isma'il ibn Salim said: I mentioned this to Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said Ibn Ashwa' told him that the Prophet had only asked the heir to pardon the man, but he refused.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I read to Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that two women from Hudhayl fought, and one caused the other's fetus to be miscarried. The Prophet ruled that compensation for it was a male or female slave.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ruled concerning the fetus of a woman from Banu Lihyan, which was miscarried dead, that compensation was a male or female slave. Then the woman against whom this compensation had been ordered died, and the Messenger of Allah ruled that her inheritance went to her children and husband, and that the blood-money was owed by her paternal relatives.

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb narrated to us. Another chain: Harmalah ibn Yahya al-Tujibi narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah said: Two women from Hudhayl fought. One threw a stone at the other, killing her and the child in her womb. They brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah, who ruled that compensation for her fetus was a male or female slave, and that the woman's blood-money was owed by her clan. He gave her children and those with them a share of her inheritance. Hamal ibn al-Nabighah al-Hudhali said, Messenger of Allah, how can I pay compensation for one who neither drank, ate, spoke, nor cried at birth? Such a case should be disregarded. The Messenger of Allah said this was one of the brothers of soothsayers, because of his rhymed speech.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Two women fought. He related the story, but did not mention that he gave her children and those with them her inheritance. He said that someone asked how they could be liable for the blood-money. He did not name Hamal ibn Malik.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Ubayd ibn Nudaylah al-Khuza'i, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: A woman struck her co-wife with a tent pole while she was pregnant and killed her. One of the women was from Lihyan. The Messenger of Allah made the slain woman's blood-money payable by the killer's clan and awarded a male or female slave for the fetus. A man from the killer's clan said, Are we to pay compensation for one who neither ate, drank, nor cried at birth? Such a case should be disregarded. The Messenger of Allah said, Is this rhymed speech like the rhyming of the Bedouins? He then made them liable for the blood-money.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Mufaddal narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Ubayd ibn Nudaylah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah: A woman killed her co-wife with a tent pole. The matter was brought to the Messenger of Allah, who ruled that her clan owed the blood-money. She was pregnant, and he ruled that compensation for the fetus was a male or female slave. Some of her clan asked whether they should pay compensation for one who neither tasted food, drank, nor cried at birth, saying such a case should be disregarded. He replied, This is rhymed speech like the rhyming of the Bedouins.

Muhammad ibn Hatim and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me; they said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, with this chain, with the meaning of the hadith of Jarir and Mufaddal.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, with their chain, relating the story. This version says that she miscarried and the matter was referred to the Prophet, who awarded a male or female slave and made it payable by the woman's heirs. This report does not mention the woman's blood-money.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. The wording is Abu Bakr's. Ishaq said: Waki' informed us; the other two said: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab consulted the people about a woman who miscarried. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah said, I witnessed the Prophet rule concerning it that compensation be a male or female slave. 'Umar said, Bring someone to testify with you. Muhammad ibn Maslamah then testified for him.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us. The wording is Yahya's. Ibn Abi 'Umar said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us; the other two said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah would cut off a thief's hand for a quarter of a dinar or more.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; they said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Kathir and Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, all of them from al-Zuhri, with the like of it through this chain.

Abu al-Tahir, Harmalah ibn Yahya, and al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to me. The wording is al-Walid's and Harmalah's. They said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah and 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: A thief's hand is not cut off unless the stolen amount is a quarter of a dinar or more.

Abu al-Tahir, Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli, and Ahmad ibn 'Isa narrated to me. The wording is Harun's and Ahmad's. Abu al-Tahir said: Ibn Wahb informed us; the other two said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Makhramah informed me, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'Amrah, who heard 'A'ishah say that she heard the Messenger of Allah say: The hand is not cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or more.

Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-'Abdi narrated to me: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Had, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, who heard the Prophet say: A thief's hand is not cut off unless the stolen amount is a quarter of a dinar or more.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, all from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far, a descendant of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, narrated to us: Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Had narrated to us with this chain, with the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: A thief's hand was not cut off during the Messenger of Allah's time for less than the price of a shield, whether a small shield or a large one; both had value.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman and Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us. Another chain: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us. All of them reported from Hisham with this chain, like the hadith of Ibn Numayr from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi. In the report of 'Abd al-Rahim and Abu Usamah it adds: and it had value at that time.
Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah cut off a thief's hand for a shield valued at three dirhams.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Ibn Rumh narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd. Another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; they said: Yahya, meaning al-Qattan, narrated to us. Another chain: Ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us. Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us. All of them reported from 'Ubaydullah. Another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma'il, meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah, narrated to us. Another chain: Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated to us; they said: Hammad narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, Ayyub ibn Musa, and Isma'il ibn Umayyah. Another chain: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me: Abu Nu'aym informed us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, Isma'il ibn Umayyah, 'Ubaydullah, and Musa ibn 'Uqbah. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Isma'il ibn Umayyah informed me. Another chain: Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan al-Jumahi, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, Malik ibn Anas, and Usamah ibn Zayd al-Laythi, all from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, with the like of Yahya's hadith from Malik. Some said its value, and some said its price: three dirhams.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us; they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: May Allah curse the thief: he steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and he steals a rope and his hand is cut off.

'Amr al-Naqid, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and 'Ali ibn Khashram narrated to us, all reporting from 'Isa ibn Yunus, from al-A'mash, with this chain, with the like of it, except that he said: If he steals a rope or an egg.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that the Quraysh were concerned about the Makhzumi woman who had stolen. They asked who would speak to the Messenger of Allah about her, and said that only Usamah, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah, would dare. Usamah spoke to him. The Messenger of Allah asked whether he was interceding concerning one of Allah's limits. Then he stood and addressed the people: The people before you were destroyed because when a high-ranking person stole, they let him go, but when a weak person stole, they carried out the prescribed punishment. By Allah, if Fatimah daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand. Ibn Rumh's report says: The people before you were destroyed.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me. The wording is Harmalah's. They said: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, from 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet, that the Quraysh were concerned about the woman who had stolen during the Prophet's time in the year of the conquest. They asked who would speak to the Messenger of Allah about her, and said that only Usamah ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah, would dare. She was brought to the Messenger of Allah, and Usamah spoke to him about her. The Messenger of Allah's face changed color and he asked whether Usamah interceded concerning one of Allah's limits. Usamah asked him to seek forgiveness for him. That evening the Messenger of Allah stood, praised Allah as He deserves, and said: The people before you were destroyed because when a high-ranking person stole, they let him go, but when a weak person stole, they carried out the prescribed punishment. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if Fatimah daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand. Then he ordered that the woman's hand be cut off. Yunus said: Ibn Shihab said: 'Urwah said: 'A'ishah said: Afterward she repented well and married. She used to visit me, and I would take her requests to the Messenger of Allah.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: A Makhzumi woman used to borrow goods and deny having them. The Prophet ordered that her hand be cut off. Her family went to Usamah ibn Zayd and asked him to speak to the Messenger of Allah on her behalf. He then related something like the hadith of al-Layth and Yunus.

Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to me: al-Hasan ibn A'yan narrated to us: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, that a woman from Banu Makhzum stole and was brought to the Prophet. She sought protection through Umm Salamah, the Prophet's wife. The Prophet said: By Allah, if it were Fatimah, I would cut off her hand. Then her hand was cut off.

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Mansur, from al-Hasan, from Hittan ibn 'Abdullah al-Raqashi, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Take it from me, take it from me: Allah has made a way for them. For an unmarried man and an unmarried woman: one hundred lashes and exile for a year. For a previously married man and a previously married woman: one hundred lashes and stoning.
